study.title: Machine learning-enabled prediction of hemorrhagic transformation post-thrombectomy using quantitative DSA

imaging.modality_detail: Quantitative DSA (qDSA); immediate post-thrombectomy anteroposterior and lateral angiograms after ICA injection (4 mL/s, 6 mL), 4 frames per second
imaging.territory_detail: Anterior circulation (ICA C2/C7, MCA M1/M3, ACA A1) after mechanical thrombectomy for large-vessel occlusion

annotation.annotator_expertise: Two neuroradiologists with >5 years of interventional experience (ROI placement), third senior neuroradiologist (>10 years) for consensus; HT labels from 6-hour post-MT CT
annotation.inter_rater_value: ICC > 0.75 for TDC-derived features; inter-observer discrepancies in <=3% of cases

task.task_description: Prediction of hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy using hemodynamic features (TTP, MTT, FWHM, WIS, WOS, stasis index) derived from gamma-variate-fitted time-density curves of post-procedural DSA, alone and combined with clinical features, using feature selection and classical machine learning classifiers.
task.clinical_application: Early risk stratification for post-thrombectomy hemorrhagic transformation in acute ischemic stroke to guide blood pressure, antiplatelet management and follow-up CT

temporal_evidence.quote: a time-density curve (TDC) was generated from the data within these regions. The TDC was then fitted using a gamma variate function

method.class_imbalance_handling: Stratified train/test splitting (StratifiedShuffleSplit) preserving class proportions

comparators: Clinical-only multivariate logistic regression (age, NIHSS, thrombectomy attempts)

G1.quote: Future multi-center studies with larger sample sizes are needed to validate the predictive performance of our models.

G2.quote: the retrospective design and single-center nature of the study may limit the generalizability of our findings.

G6.quote: Firstly, the retrospective design and single-center nature of the study may limit the generalizability of our findings.

G7.quote: SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation.

G8.quote: By integrating clinical and hemodynamic features, machine learning algorithms can be effectively utilized to construct a preliminary predictive model for post-thrombectomy HT

G9.quote: In our study, there were relatively few cases with eTICI grade 2b, while most were grade 2C or 3.

G11.quote: This study aims to construct a predictive model for post-thrombectomy hemorrhagic transformation (HT) by integrating hemodynamic features derived from quantitative DSA (qDSA) with machine learning models.

other_limitations: No subgroup analysis by eTICI grade
Patients with large-area infarction or cerebral herniation excluded
Statistical bias from p < 0.1 threshold in univariate clinical feature selection
future_work: Multi-center validation with larger sample sizes
Subgroup analyses and separate models by eTICI grade
Three-category study including large infarction and herniation outcomes
Study of postoperative blood pressure control in high-risk patients
